title: Action Cycles
summary: Action Cycles was a series of larger-scale (approximately 1:12-1:18 scale) Hot Wheels motorcycles produced from 1987 to about 1997/98, initially under the Hot Wheels Giants line. These were a series of Hot Wheels cars which featured clockwork motors which could be activated by pulling back and releasing, akin to many other clockwork toy cars....

title: Sizzlers
summary: right|300pxSizzlers was a line of motorized Hot Wheels cars produced from 1970 to 1978. The line was engineered by George Soulakis, who also recommended the TampoPrint process to apply tampos on Hot Wheels cars.

title: Hot Wheels Elite 1:18 Scale
summary: This is a 1:18 scale series of Hot Wheels cars under the Hot Wheels Elite branding produced from 2006 to 2015. Most castings from 2006 to 2011 have a limited production run of between 5,000 and 10,000. Some models are part of the "Super Elite" line with a significantly reduced production run.

title: Hudson
summary: The Hudson Motor Car Company made Hudson and other branded automobiles in Detroit, Michigan, and abroad, from 1909 until 1954. In 1954, Hudson merged with Nash-Kelvinator to form American Motors Corporation (AMC). The Hudson name was marketed through the 1957 model year, after which it was discontinued.

title: Holden
summary: Holden, formerly known as General Motors-Holden, was an Australian subsidiary company of General Motors. Founded in Adelaide, it was an automobile manufacturer, importer, and exporter that sold cars under its own marque in Australia. It was headquartered in Port Melbourne, with major industrial operations in the states of South Australia and Victoria.
